title: console-observability-triage-scratchpad-noah-2026-03-07
content:
Quick triage scratchpad - doing the morning pass on console/observability issues.

Summary of today
- Two customer reports overnight about missing widget data on the `model-latency` dashboard. Appears intermittent (15-60m windows).
- PagerDuty page at 03:12 UTC (PD: #1298) for spike in 99th pct latency for hosted-prod-us-west. Auto-resolved after 20m.
- Alert flapping: `dashboard-render-error` firing ~every 40m for dashboards backed by metrics/renderer-service.

Initial checks (what I ran)
- Looked at dashboard logs (renderer-service) between 02:45-04:00 UTC: repeated 500s when query payload > ~15000 chars (likely large graph queries).
- Cross-checked metrics ingestion: no gaps in series; prometheus remote write healthy.
- Verified query layer (thanos/query) had elevated memory usage around the same windows. Thanos pod restarted once at 03:05 UTC (OOMKilled).
- Client-side (console) stack traces show `RequestTimeout` on fetch of /api/dashboard-data at 03:18 UTC from customer a-corp (CS-3321).

Immediate hypotheses
- Large dashboards with many panels -> heavy queries -> query layer OOM -> intermittent 500s and high p99 latency.
- Renderer service might be timing out on long queries; error bubbling up to dashboard UI.
- Possible correlation with a recent rollout of query-cache config on 2026-03-05 (rollout id: rollout-obs-querycache-2026-03-05) — check rollout and canary metrics.

Repro steps to try locally/cluster
1) Recreate heavy dashboard query payload (from customer CS-3321 screenshot) using curl against /api/dashboard-data with same time range and panel config. See if renderer returns 500.
2) Patch query to use smaller time range / remove heavy agg -> should succeed.
3) Scale up thanos-query to +1 replica in staging and run load test to confirm memory pressure replicates.

Notes / Logs to capture
- Renderer service logs: filter for error message `failed to render panel` and capture stack traces.
- Thanos pod restart events (kube events) and memory RSS prior to OOM.
- Dashboard request IDs from console traces to map to backend logs (trace id mapping).

Action items (owner, ETA)
- [Noah] Create an incident summary message for CS and link to CS-3321 (ETA: 30m) -> notify CS and customer a-corp with interim note.
- [Jordan] Rollback or throttle rollout `rollout-obs-querycache-2026-03-05` in canary if metrics show degradation (ETA: 1h).
- [Chris] Add temporary rate-limiter on renderer queries > 10000 chars to avoid OOMs and surface helpful error to UI (ETA: EOD).
- [Aisha] Confirm whether we auto-scale thanos-query on memory pressure; propose HPA rule if not (ETA: tomorrow).

Customer comms
- CS ticket CS-3321: Suggested a temporary workaround to reduce time-range on the affected dashboard; recommend they pin a smaller window or use aggregated panels until fix.
- Note to include: we are treating as P2 until we confirm customer-facing degradation consistent/ongoing.

Follow-ups to log in Jira / Confluence
- Create OBS-1245 (root cause investigation) and attach logs + heap dumps (if available).
- Update confluence page Dashboard+Design+Notes with guidance on query size limits and recommended panel design for customers.

Other TODOs / scratch notes
- Check if `renderer-service` memory limits were recently lowered in k8s resource update 2026-03-01 (k8s PR #4567).
- Run `grafana-dashboard-audit` script to find dashboards with > 50 panels or nested queries. Make list and reach out to owners.
- Add a short alerting rule for thanos-query memory > 75% over 5m with runbook link.

Raw snippets / queries to paste elsewhere
- Example curl payload: { query: "panel=34&from=1677600000&to=1677603600&vars=..." } (replace with real panel payload).
- Kube get events: kubectl -n monitoring get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | grep thanos

Quick notes to self
- If we hit a recurring OOM, take thanos-query out of rotation before restart to prevent cascading failures.
- Keep CS looped in; avoid promising ETA until we have root cause.

End-of-pass checklist
- [ ] Incident summary posted to #obs-incident with link to OBS-1245
- [ ] CS updated on workaround and we captured console trace IDs
- [ ] Thanos OOM evidence captured (pod logs + metrics snapshot)

-- Noah B.
(working notes — will clean up and move key items to OBS-1245 and slack updates)
